papers.title: Germline EGFR T790M mutation and lung cancer risk.
papers.summary: Across more than 3.3 million individuals, the germline EGFR T790M variant is significantly associated with lung cancer risk — exceeding smoking-attributable risk and several-fold higher in never-smokers — with no elevated risk for 17 other cancers. Higher US prevalence reflects a southern Appalachian founder event ~200–225 years ago, informing targeted testing and screening.

papers.title: Ancient DNA unveils distinctive ancestries in the Bronze and Iron Ages of East Tianshan.
papers.summary: Genome-wide data from 135 ancient individuals across 11 East Tianshan sites reveal a previously unrecognized Bronze Age admixture between Yellow River millet farmers and Chemurchek-related steppe pastoralists, little input from later steppe groups, and increasing Iron Age heterogeneity — documenting sustained demographic interaction in eastern Central Asia ~1,800 years before the Silk Road.

papers.title: Multi-organelle signatures map cell-state diversity and metabolic adaptation in tissues.
papers.summary: Spatial organellomics combines automated segmentation with machine learning to classify cell states from multi-organelle signatures in tissue. In liver, hepatocytes form intermixed communities within canonical zones, refining the subzonal diversity model. Fasting-induced organelle remodeling, linked intravitally to altered mitochondrial membrane potential, marks multi-organelle architecture as a structural readout of metabolic adaptation.

papers.title: Splenic regulation of systemic platelet activation state.
papers.summary: In mice, the spleen filters activated platelets during thrombosis and inflammation, maintaining platelet quiescence. GPVI-dependent activation in the red pulp is counterbalanced by perlecan-triggered G6B-b inhibitory signaling, letting quiescent platelets recirculate, while preactivated platelets are captured via inside-out signaling and β1-integrin engagement. The spleen thus modulates systemic platelet responsiveness and thrombo-inflammatory risk.

papers.title: A noncontiguous code for RNA-guided DNA recognition at the origin of CRISPR-Cas.
papers.summary: Viral interference programmable repeat (VIPR) systems comprise a protein ancestral to the earliest CRISPR-Cas effectors and vrRNAs with alternating GGY/NN motifs. Unlike canonical guides, vrRNAs recognize double-stranded DNA noncontiguously, with variable dinucleotides specifying a gapped target. Natural targets indicate anti-phage activity, and redirected complexes confer programmable phage defense via transcriptional repression.

papers.title: Transcriptome-based classification in mice with ASD-risk mutations.
papers.summary: A sex-balanced atlas of 1,008 prefrontal RNA-seq profiles from 17 mouse lines carrying ASD-risk mutations identifies two opposing transcriptomic states differing in sex bias, regional specificity, developmental stability, cell-type remodeling, and fluoxetine/lithium responses. Single-nucleus profiling shows broader remodeling in group 1, supporting molecular stratification with conserved synaptic directionality across independent lines.

papers.title: VIPR RNA-guided DNA recognition by noncontiguous geometric triplex formation.
papers.summary: Twenty-one cryo-EM structures show VIPR protomers oligomerizing along the vrRNA into a right-handed helical filament that sequesters GGY motifs and positions adjacent NN bases for target pairing. DNA binding skips every third nucleotide, forming a gapped hybrid helix that encircles the nontarget strand — a geometric triplex enabling noncontiguous RNA-guided DNA recognition.

papers.title: A Molecularly Anchored Spatial Transcriptomic Framework for Precise CA1-Subiculum Parcellation and Region-Resolved Analysis in Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.summary: Using Stereo-seq and single-nucleus RNA-seq references from 12 human donors, this framework defines reproducible molecular boundaries between hippocampal CA1 and subiculum. FN1 and ETV1 mark subicular identity across datasets. Applied to Alzheimer's tissue, it reveals region-specific transcriptional alterations, including enriched mitochondrial energy metabolism transcripts in the subiculum.

papers.title: Local ancestry inference identifies robust evidence of selection in Neolithic Europe.
papers.summary: Benchmarking eight local ancestry inference methods on 176 imputed Neolithic genomes shows ancestry estimates correlate across methods, but tract lengths and admixture times vary by an order of magnitude. A robust FADS1/2 selection signal replicates across two independent datasets, while HLA signals appear method-biased — underscoring multi-method validation.

papers.title: A CsWRKY46-CsPBL9-CsARI1 tripartite regulatory module coordinates H(2)O(2) production and callose deposition in citrus fruit immunity.
papers.summary: Citrus fruit immunity is coordinated by a tripartite module: CsWRKY46 transcriptionally activates the H2O2-producing CsRbohG and callose-synthase CsCalS5; CsPBL9 phosphorylation enhances CsRbohG activity; and the E3 ligase CsARI1 ubiquitinates both as an immune brake. CsARI1 also moonlights, binding CsPBL9 in an H2O2-stimulated feedback loop that disrupts CsRbohG activation.

papers.title: Albumin uptake through FcRn promotes tumor-associated macrophage maturation and albumin-bound immunotherapy response.
papers.summary: Tumor-associated macrophages are the dominant nonmalignant albumin-accumulating cells in mouse tumors. FcRn mediates myeloid-intrinsic albumin uptake driving monocyte-to-TAM maturation via p62-NRF2 signaling; albumin deficiency or FcRn loss reduces TAMs. Albumin conjugation prolongs STING-agonist circulation and improves antitumor efficacy, establishing albumin as an endogenous regulator of myeloid-directed immunotherapy response.

papers.title: Colony morphogenesis regulates sporulation dynamics in bacterial biofilms.
papers.summary: In Bacillus subtilis biofilms, an early, high-frequency sporulation wave drives the colony toward dormancy from within while a narrow non-sporulating edge maintains expansion. Mutants and modeling show faster-spreading biofilms spatially separate growth from sporulation, demonstrating that collective morphogenesis patterns cell differentiation across scales in multicellular bacterial colonies.

papers.title: Spontaneous lytic reactivation drives a persistent B cell-vector pathway for epithelial dissemination of the Epstein-Barr virus.
papers.summary: Using an induction-free primary B cell system, this study shows carcinoma-associated EBV strains transmit to epithelial cells far more efficiently than lymphoid strains. Transmission requires spontaneous lytic reactivation, viral DNA replication, and de novo virions, with GH/GL engagement of EPHA2/desmocollin-2 and actin/PI3K-dependent endocytosis. Infected B cells retain transmission capacity for months.

papers.title: A yeast model for the functional analysis of SRP54 mutations associated with severe congenital neutropenia.
papers.summary: A engineered yeast strain whose growth depends on hormone-inducible SRP54 recapitulates dominant-negative phenotypes of severe congenital neutropenia mutations: S125del shows the mildest growth defect and G234E the most severe, matching clinical severity. The authors characterize four previously unreported clinical mutations and present the first X-ray structure of yeast SRP54, enabling high-throughput screening.

papers.title: Arginine Kinase 1 supports energy homeostasis in Drosophila flight muscle development.
papers.summary: Arginine kinase 1 (ArgK1), the sole phosphagen kinase expressed during Drosophila flight muscle development, localizes to mitochondria in developing myofibers. Muscle-specific depletion lowers ATP and the NAD+/NADH ratio, abolishes spontaneous contractions required for sarcomere maturation, and disrupts mitochondrial morphogenesis — establishing ArgK1 as essential for energy homeostasis during myofibrillogenesis and muscle growth.

papers.title: Parallel regulation of tissue morphogenesis and cell fate specification by RAR:RXR signalling during pancreas formation.
papers.summary: In a new hESC organoid model of pancreas formation, RAR:RXR signaling induces both pancreatic budding and cell fate specification through β-catenin. Membrane β-catenin reduction weakens cell-cell adhesion, perturbing apical-basal polarity, while nuclear depletion relieves repression of FOXA2-dependent PDX1 transcription — a framework for how developmental cues coordinate morphogenesis and specification.

papers.title: Epistasis and the changing fitness landscapes of SARS-CoV-2.
papers.summary: Comparing inferred spike-protein fitness landscapes across SARS-CoV-2 variants reveals that mutation fitness effects shift with genetic background. Sites with altered costs cluster near residues that differ between variants. A pairwise epistasis model explains about half the variance in these shifts, with each mismatched residue affecting mutation effects at typically one to three additional positions.

papers.title: Genetic principles enabling the creation of bacteria-based therapeutics.
papers.summary: This review outlines genetic design principles for bacteria-based therapeutics: chassis selection, attenuation and biocontainment, control of therapeutic activity, targeting and persistence, and genotype-to-phenotype stability. It examines liabilities — off-target behavior, unstable expression, and evolutionary loss of function — and highlights engineered Salmonella, E. coli, Listeria, and Yersinia candidates, including bacteria delivering complete gene editing systems.

papers.title: Highly Contiguous Is Not Chromosomally Accurate: Integrated Cytogenetic and Genomic Mapping in Two Turtle Genome.
papers.summary: Integrating comparative chromosome painting, chromosome-specific probes, and synteny analysis in two turtle species shows highly contiguous assemblies can misrepresent chromosome structure. The loggerhead sea turtle assembly is largely consistent, with two under-assembled microchromosomes, while the red-eared slider assembly shows cytogenetically detectable discrepancies — supporting routine cytogenetic validation and reference genome updates.

papers.title: The COP9 signalosome subunit CSN1 regulates glioblastoma stem cell growth.
papers.summary: Using patient-derived glioblastoma stem cell lines, CSN1 is identified as the crucial COP9 signalosome subunit for growth: knockout disrupts cell-cycle transcriptional programs, activates apoptosis, and significantly extends survival in orthotopic xenografts. Mechanistically, CSN1 is required for signalosome complex assembly and regulates AP-1 activation through JNK1/2/3 and c-Jun phosphorylation.

papers.title: A segmentation-guided CNN-Vision transformer feature fusion framework for multi-class breast ultrasound image classification.
papers.summary: This framework segments breast lesions with a fusion-enhanced transformer U-Net, extracts and fuses CNN and vision-transformer features from the segmented regions, and classifies benign, malignant, and normal images via a dense-layer network. On the BUSI dataset (780 images), it achieves 95.11% accuracy, 95.66% sensitivity, 97.63% specificity, and F1 0.945.

papers.title: Computational screening of oncogenic genetic variations in tumor suppressor proteins driving gastric cancer pathogenesis.
papers.summary: A deep learning graph neural network identified 1,886 gastric cancer genes with both differential expression and high mutation propensity. TP53 was the top hub (47.6% mutation frequency), followed by ERBB2, CDH1, and APC. cBioPortal validation confirmed 36 missense SNPs affecting modification sites and 60 nonsense SNPs, with altered survival associations.

papers.title: Isoquercitrin ameliorates chondrocyte dysfunction in osteoarthritis by targeting AKT1-mediated mitochondrial dynamics regulation.
papers.summary: Isoquercitrin (IQ) counters IL-1β-induced chondrocyte proliferation arrest, shifts metabolism toward anabolism, reduces pro-inflammatory responses, and restores mitochondrial dynamic balance in osteoarthritis models. IQ binds AKT1 with high affinity, and AKT1 overexpression abolishes its protective effects, confirming AKT1-mediated mitochondrial dynamics regulation as the mechanistic basis for IQ's chondroprotection.

papers.title: A trainable language model with potential to modulate translation rates in non-model organisms by generating upstream untranslated region sequence libraries.
papers.summary: A sliding-window n-gram language model trained on an organism's native 5'-UTR sequences generates synthetic library variants preserving organism-specific statistics without mechanistic assumptions. Libraries for E. coli and L. reuteri (~1,000 sequences each, ~100 tested) yielded broad translation levels; cross-species performance correlated weakly, and thermodynamic predictions showed little predictive power, especially in the non-model host.

papers.title: Integrated bioinformatics analysis of chromosomal deletion regions in glioblastoma identifies key genes linked to GABA(A) receptor signaling.
papers.summary: Bioinformatic analysis of glioblastoma deletion regions identified 1,704 differentially expressed genes and 11 downregulated hub genes spanning the entire GABA(A) receptor complex. Mutations in CACNA1D, GABRA1, and GABRB2 are predicted to disrupt protein structure and function, and molecular dynamics of meprobamate binding support GABA(A) receptors as potential tumor-suppressive targets in glioblastoma.

papers.title: Hyperbaric Oxygen Treatment Enhances Definitive Endoderm Differentiation and Hepatic Maturation of Human-Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells in Association with mTORC2-Dependent AKT Phosphorylation.
papers.summary: Hyperbaric oxygen treatment during definitive endoderm differentiation of hiPSCs increases DE markers (SOX17, GATA4, FOXA2, CXCR4), with two sessions optimal. HBOT-induced AKT Ser473 phosphorylation is incompletely blocked by PI3K inhibition but reduced by torin2, implicating mTORC2. Resulting hepatocyte-like cells show elevated albumin, AFP, HNF4A, and asialoglycoprotein receptor expression.

papers.title: From scissors to editors: how the evolution of precision is redefining therapeutic genome editing.
papers.summary: This review traces CRISPR's evolution from bacterial immunity to precision medicine, covering early Cas9 systems' off-target effects and variable editing outcomes, and subsequent refinements toward greater specificity, safety, and predictability. Persistent challenges include off-target editing, delivery inefficiencies, and ethical questions of accessibility and long-term consequences for therapeutic genome editing.

papers.title: USP22 alleviates oxidative stress-induced BMSCs senescence by stabilizing SPI1 protein.
papers.summary: In H2O2-treated bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells and an ovariectomy-induced osteoporotic rat model, SPI1 declines with senescence. SPI1 overexpression rescues senescence and osteogenic impairment by transcriptionally activating NAMPT and elevating NAD+. USP22 deubiquitinates and stabilizes SPI1; USP22 overexpression alleviates senescence, an effect reversed by SPI1 knockdown.

papers.title: L-Cysteine and N-Acetylcysteine Supplementation Improves Clinical Outcome in a Patient With COXPD10.
papers.journal: American journal of medical genetics. Part A
papers.summary: Biallelic MTO1 variants cause COXPD10, a mitochondrial translation disorder with severe infantile hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and lactic acidosis. MTO1 modifies mitochondrial tRNAs using taurine from cysteine metabolism. A 22-month-old child, diagnosed early with a severe genotype and treated with L-cysteine and N-acetylcysteine, did not develop cardiac manifestations — suggesting early disease-specific treatment benefits.

papers.title: Moebius-Plus Phenotype With Positive RCEM Episignature May Indicate Broader Embryologic Malformation Spectrum Detectable by Methylation Profiling.
papers.journal: American journal of medical genetics. Part A
papers.summary: An 8-month-old with clinical Moebius syndrome and nondiagnostic genome sequencing showed a moderately positive RCEM DNA methylation episignature, concordant with two of three validated RCEM classifiers. This first reported RCEM-positive Moebius case suggests a shared embryologic malformation spectrum, positioning episignature testing as a diagnostic tool when conventional genomic testing is unrevealing.

papers.title: Comparison of manual counting with two rule-based image analysis programs, ImageJ and CellProfiler, for quantitative analysis of c-Fos immunohistochemical positivity in rat brainstem sections.
papers.journal: Biotechnic & histochemistry : official publication of the Biological Stain Commission
papers.summary: Comparing manual counting with ImageJ and CellProfiler for c-Fos immunohistochemical positivity across 124 rat brainstem images found no statistically significant differences (Friedman p = 0.07). Inter-observer and inter-method agreement were excellent (ICCs 0.96–0.98), with small mean biases and no proportional bias, supporting rule-based image analysis as an accessible, reliable alternative.
